chain.label: IMC with low ceiling and fog at destination
chain.trigger: Instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) prevailed at the time of the accident; overcast ceiling at 400-600 feet with patchy fog and mist

chain.label: Bull Mountain rises along the missed approach flightpath
chain.trigger: crashed into mountainous terrain in Stuart, Virginia... on Bull Mountain... near the extended centerline of the runway

chain.label: GPS database expired and not IFR-certified
chain.trigger: The GPS database was not current and therefore was not certified for IFR navigation.

chain.label: Company deferred EGPWS installation to sister aircraft
chain.trigger: the accident airplane was 'put back out on the line' and was scheduled for a GPS upgrade and an EGPWS installation at the end of the 2004 racing season

chain.label: Crew failed to notice GPS autosequenced from BALES LOM to MTV
chain.trigger: the accident approach profile is consistent with the pilots using the GPS data to navigate to the BALES LOM and then failing to notice that the GPS had autosequenced to MTV after the airplane passed BALES

caused_by.evidence: the Bendix/King KLN 90B GPS was used for backup only and strictly for position awareness

chain.label: Approach and missed approach flown displaced from published procedure
chain.trigger: the airplane flew an approach that was displaced by about 5 nm compared with the published approach; the flight crew initiated the missed approach 7.5 nm beyond the MAP... The airplane then entered a straight-ahead climb on the runway heading

caused_by.evidence: the pilots might have mistakenly believed that the airplane was showing distance data to the BALES LOM when, in fact, the airplane was showing distance data to MTV

chain.label: Controlled flight into Bull Mountain terrain
chain.trigger: The accident occurred on Bull Mountain in Stuart, Virginia, at an elevation of about 2,400 feet and near the extended centerline of the runway.

caused_by.evidence: Interpolation of nominal climb rates and a standard turn rate depicted a flightpath that would have kept the airplane clear of terrain
the accident occurred on Bull Mountain... near the extended centerline of the runway
Bull Mountain was completely obscured by clouds and fog... visibility was between 0 and 0.25 mile
The airplane was not equipped with an enhanced ground proximity warning system (EGPWS).

chain.label: Fatal injuries to all ten occupants
chain.trigger: The two flight crewmembers and eight passengers were killed, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces and postcrash fire.

caused_by.evidence: The two flight crewmembers and eight passengers were killed
